title: Module 9 · Lesson 1 — Guardrails and the five rail types

lines: Welcome to Module Nine, Lesson One: guardrails and the five rail types.
Guardrails are runtime checks between your app and the model.
Picture PetPal, an online pet pharmacy whose support agent can issue refunds.
In its first week, three things go wrong.

say.0: Picture Pet Pal, an online pet pharmacy whose support agent can issue refunds.

lines: It happily compares prices with a rival store.
Then someone talks it into a nine-hundred-dollar refund.
It even repeats a stranger's address from a retrieved note.
The only control was a polite line in the prompt.
Guardrails put checks at five points around the model.
NeMo Guardrails calls them the input, dialog, retrieval, execution, and output rails.
The input rail runs before the model sees the user's message.
It catches jailbreaks, redacts personal data, and restricts topics.
The dialog rail keeps conversations on approved paths.
The retrieval rail screens retrieved chunks for sensitive or injected text before they enter the prompt.
The execution rail wraps every tool call.
It restricts which tools may run, validates arguments, and requires approval for high-impact actions.
The output rail checks the response before the user sees it.
It filters toxicity and personal data, checks grounding, and enforces format.
So for PetPal, competitor questions hit the input rail, and big refunds the execution rail.
The leaked address belongs on the retrieval rail, with output as a backstop.

say.0: So for Pet Pal, competitor questions hit the input rail, and big refunds the execution rail.

lines: Rails are written in Colang, as user intents, bot responses, and flows.
If you see define user or define flow, think NeMo Guardrails.
But guardrails are one layer, not the whole answer.
Defence in depth stacks independent controls, because any one can fail.
For a sensitive action, name an input rail, server-side tool permissions, and approval on the risky step.
Add an output rail and an audit record.
Rails add latency, since some checks are model calls.
Run cheap checks like regex and allow-lists first, and save model checks for judgement.
On the exam, expect one requirement with all five rails as options.
Ask where the check must run, then read on.
